guide.summary: Agent acting in customers' Kintone domains (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio lists Kintone REST under 'Bring your own OAuth app', so you must supply your own client ID and secret in an auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for Kintone REST, so you must register your own OAuth client in Kintone and put its credentials in a Composio auth config.
reasons: No managed OAuth app exists for Kintone in Composio
Users see your client name on the Kintone consent screen
Your own app gets dedicated quota instead of shared quota

scenarios.label: Agent acting in customers' Kintone domains
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects to end users' Kintone domains. An admin of each domain registers the OAuth client and enables users.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured; see c1, c13.

waiting.basis: No provider review is described in the docs (c1, c5).

extras: Admin registers client and enables each user

prerequisites.title: Kintone admin access
prerequisites.detail: Only common administrators can add OAuth clients. For testing, the Developer Program gives a free 1-year developer license.

prerequisites.title: Redirect URI from Composio
prerequisites.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. It is required when registering the client.

steps.title: Decide scopes to request
steps.detail: Map agent features to scopes such as k:app_record:read and k:app_record:write. Separate multiple scopes with spaces.
steps.done_when: A minimal scope list is written down

steps.title: Register OAuth client in Kintone
steps.detail: In System Administration, open OAuth and click Add OAuth Client. Enter a client name and the redirect endpoint from Composio, then Save.
steps.done_when: Client ID, secret and endpoints are shown

steps.title: Enable client for users
steps.detail: Use Configure users to tick each user allowed to use the client. New users start unchecked.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a kintone_rest auth config through Composio's API with the client ID, secret and subdomain endpoints.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Log in to Kintone, approve the request, and confirm a tool call works.

traps.title: Users disabled by default
traps.detail: A new client works for no one until an admin ticks users, and new Kintone users are unchecked too.

traps.title: IP restrictions block OAuth
traps.detail: Domains using IP restrictions must allowlist the OAuth client's IP, or OAuth fails.

traps.title: Client registered per domain
traps.detail: The client lives in a Kintone domain and its endpoints use that subdomain. Expect one registration per customer domain, with a limit of 20 clients per domain.

traps.title: Short-lived tokens, limited refresh tokens
traps.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and authorization codes 10 minutes. Refresh tokens do not expire, but only 10 are allowed per client per user.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The redirect_uri in the token request must equal the one in the authorization request.

blockers.what_it_means: The user is not ticked in Configure users for that client.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the domain admin to enable the user.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the instructions for the admin.

blockers.symptom: Access token calls fail with errors
blockers.what_it_means: The token expired (1 hour) or the scope does not cover the API.
blockers.what_to_do: Refresh the token and check the granted scopes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the API called against granted scopes.

open_questions: Can one OAuth client serve many customer domains, or must each domain register its own? Check with Kintone developer support or test with a second domain.
Is there any marketplace or listing review for Kintone integrations? No review was found; confirm with Kintone partner pages.
Do customers' Kintone licences or plans affect API access? Not found; ask Kintone sales or support.
